chunks: My father - may God be pleased with him - narrated: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Hamran, from Khaysamah who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me:
"Visit each other in your homes, for that is the revival of our affair. May God have mercy on a servant who revives our affair."

key_terms.أَمْرِنَا: Our affair (referring to the Imams' cause/teachings)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of visiting each other in homes according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights this narration to emphasize that social cohesion among the faithful is not merely customary but a vital mechanism for sustaining the spiritual authority of the Imams. This practice of *tizawwur* (mutual visiting) is presented as a means of reviving the 'Amr' (affair/command) of the Imams, ensuring their teachings remain active and relevant in the community's daily life. The supplication for mercy underscores the high spiritual status of those who actively preserve this bond, linking individual piety to collective religious vitality.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 1-77 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim quoted on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Hamran, on the authority of Khaysamat that Abu Ja’far al-Baqir (MGB) told him,
“Visit each other in your homes since this will revive our affairs - may God forgive anyone who revives our affairs.”
